prose_updates.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. A one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) gives the exact separation \(9/70>9/91\); strict interiority and continuity extend it to a nonempty open neighborhood with a uniformly positive gap. On a named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, a uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws; a contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's equations~(10), (12), and (14) provide an observed-policy-first divergence and Jensen--CMC computation, but the resulting armwise weights need not be realizable by one cross-world-compatible assignment law. Existing work therefore neither supplies the one-way full-law embedding on the same Neyman budget scale nor establishes an exact and open-set strict cost gap. Existing inference theory also does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes make the missing joint law explicit, expose a response-type garbling geometry invisible to armwise reweighting, and permit an interior finite-dimensional comparison showing that the relaxation gap is robust to small changes in the observed law.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, and maps each compatible full law one way into an explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) at no greater cost. It proves the exact values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\) and, by continuity at strictly interior scalar minimizers, a uniformly positive gap on a nonempty open neighborhood. It also pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem based on a common fixed odds cone and uniformly bounded attained multipliers with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

prose_updates.related_work: Rubin supplies the potential-outcome notation and consistency framework, while Tan supplies the marginal odds-ratio sensitivity model used for the assignment restriction. Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Dorn and Guo's quantile-balancing result and Dorn, Guo, and Kallus's doubly sharp extension establish sharp worst-case marginal-sensitivity benchmarks; neither profiles one joint full-law average assignment budget. Ishikawa and He's kernel conditional-moment construction and Jin, Ren, and Zhou's general \(f\)-sensitivity model motivate tractable observed-weight relaxations, but do not impose the present cross-world-compatible joint response law. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in their equation~(10), apply Jensen in equation~(12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation~(14). The comparison here is deliberately one way: every compatible full law induces a feasible point of the note's explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization with no larger cost; no equality with their unqualified published class and no reverse cross-world realizability are claimed. The rational witness has values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\), and strict interiority of both scalar programs makes the gap uniformly positive on an open neighborhood of observed laws. Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; the binary garbling result instead derives monotone support for an extremal compatible law without assuming monotone treatment response of the population. Blackwell's comparison-of-experiments order motivates the garbling language, but does not establish preservation of the two observed causal margins and ATE proved here. The regular finite-sample theorem rescales response-type masses onto a common odds cone, derives a uniform right inverse and multiplier bound from the declared Slater margin, and compares different observed laws through the saddle identity at each law rather than reusing a moved dual certificate. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Duchi, Glynn, and Namkoong study generalized empirical-likelihood robust optimization; neither covers this support-changing extended-real profile. Fang and Santos, Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, and Masten and Poirier provide directional or breakdown-frontier inference tools, while Zhao, Small, and Bhattacharya give a bootstrap sensitivity procedure; extending such inference through this frontier's zero cells and moving faces remains open. Masten, Poirier, and Ren provide a general relaxation-of-unconfoundedness perspective, whereas the present result specializes to an attained finite full-law information frontier. Nattino, Ashmead, and Lu motivate the undeveloped complex-survey extension, and Cinelli and Hazlett motivate observed-covariate calibration; neither extension or empirical application is claimed here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, one-way cost transfer into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, exact rational separation, open-neighborhood uniform gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims proved in the note. The comparison does not identify that specialization with Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's unqualified published class and does not assert that every relaxed armwise weight is induced by a compatible cross-world assignment law. The regular diameter proof controls coefficient movement through a common fixed odds cone and a law-specific saddle comparison; it does not claim stability of an active set or feasibility of one law's dual certificate at another law. Uniform tangent inference under weaker facial regularity and adaptive derivative-bootstrap inversion remain open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target remains a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit inverse-propensity map proves a one-way inclusion and same-scale cost transfer from compatible full laws into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, while the exact rational witness quantifies the price of requiring one cross-world-compatible assignment mechanism.
statement_notes.gap: IshikawaHeKanamori2026Convex, equations~(10), (12), and (14), defines the unrelaxed \(f\)-divergence and its Jensen--CMC relaxation, but does not prove reverse cross-world realizability, the Neyman-generator full-law embedding used here, or the strict \(9/70\) versus \(9/91\) full-law ATE gap.
statement_notes.consumer: A sensitivity analyst treats the relaxed program as a one-way lower-cost screen, not as an identical feasible-law class, and avoids declaring the ATE \(3/10\) feasible at budgets between \(9/91\) and \(9/70\) for the witness law.

statement_notes.justification: Strictly interior minimizers in both finite-dimensional scalar programs make the exact witness robust: continuity preserves at least half of its rational cost gap on a nonempty open neighborhood.
statement_notes.gap: A single numerical or rational witness could be a knife-edge phenomenon; the local theorem rules this out without assuming fixed active odds faces throughout the neighborhood.
statement_notes.consumer: The comparison remains informative under small multinomial sampling perturbations of the treated fraction and the two observed arm success probabilities.
